PART B - MATERIALLY ORTHOGONAL, AND DECIDABLE FROM EVIDENCE ALREADY BANKED, SO IT COSTS NO NEW CORPUS: is a measured break-even reuse count f* even REPORTABLE by this literature class, or is its absence a property of the field's reporting convention rather than of the field's economics? arXiv:2608.05784v1 already prints the complete per-task cost model E[$/task] = (1-hq)Cmiss p + hq(Chit+Cverify) + h(1-q)Cwrong + Cwrite N (Eq. 1) with N as the reuse count, and names its own missing input in the same breath - 'the one input none of them measures is h on the pre-delegation passive corpus'. That is a ready-made sufficiency test requiring no new literature: solve Eq. (1) for f* under the paper's own published parameter ranges (R 60-343x, h 0.090 in-sample and 0.077 out-of-sample, p the base success rate, q the hit-match fraction, Cwrite the write cost, Cverify the verification cost) and report, with the algebra shown, whether f* is finite and reachable, at what reuse count, and under which parameter regimes it diverges. If f* is finite and bounded for published parameters, then a measured f* IS reportable and its absence becomes a reporting-practice finding that is decision-grade for the mandate's output contract. If f* diverges across the published parameter range, then no system in this class could report a bounded break-even, and the persistence-economics anchor is unavailable from this literature class by construction - a stronger and cheaper result than another search, and one that simultaneously tells Product what f* to measure internally and what regime to measure it in.
